day: Friday of week 24 in Ordinary Time
text:
There is something tender in the way Luke describes the disciples traveling with Jesus. Along with the Twelve are women—Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Susanna, others unnamed—walking the dusty roads, proclaiming the kingdom together. These are not distant believers. They are present. They have been healed and they have chosen to stay, to give of themselves, to journey with him.

Paul's words about resurrection can feel weighty, urgent with argument. But perhaps what he is really saying underneath is this: the hope we cling to is not reasonable by the world's measure. It rests entirely on the fact of Christ raised from death. And that hope changes everything. It changes how we travel through our own days—no longer as people merely enduring until the end, but as people walking alongside the one who has conquered death, called to share in his life now.

The women in the Gospel gave from their resources. Paul gave his witness. Both are forms of trust in a resurrection that has already begun. As you sit with these readings, you might notice what you have been given—your own healing, your own particular gifts—and what it might mean to place them in service to the kingdom that is breaking into the world. What would it look like to travel with Christ today, not as a distant hope, but as a present reality?
